transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2025-03-05 15:00 PT
- Duration: ~45 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Lin (Redwood SE), Jared (CTO NimbleHealth), Priya (Lead Eng), Marco (SRE), Alison (PM)

Summary: quick weekly check-in on POC integration. Focus on SDK function-calling, structured output stability, and perf numbers from customer test harness.

00:00 Jared: yeah thanks everyone for joining, uh we've been running the new SDK snippet you sent last week and have some results and a couple of blockers to go through
00:12 Maya: great, thanks Jared, super appreciate it, Diego and Lin from our SE team are here to go deep on the function calls and structured outputs
00:20 Priya: quick context - we integrated SDK into our recommendations service, using the function-calling path to invoke a downstream snippet generator. We're seeing two problems: first sometimes the model emits "raw text" instead of the JSON schema we expect, second latency spikes when streaming is enabled with batching
00:40 Diego: ok, got it. For the JSON emissions, are you using the SDK helper to declare the function schema and required fields? sometimes devs hand-roll the parser and that causes mismatch. Also is there any post-processing on your side?
00:55 Priya: yes we declared schema, example: name, type, items[], metadata object. But the outputs sometimes contain trailing commas or single quotes and our strict JSON parser fails. Also on the function call we see the model returning "assistant call" vs actual arguments in some responses
01:15 Lin: right, we saw a few older model-variants that had inconsistent tool-calling behavior. What model are you pinned to in the POC config?
01:25 Marco: currently pinned to redwood-model-v2-beta (we set it via the config). We also tried an open model from the catalog and saw similar but slightly less frequent schema breaks
01:40 Diego: hmmm, two levers here: 1) enforce structured output using the SDK's schema validator (we have a flag that enforces post-generation schema validation and auto-retry), 2) use function-calling strict mode which wraps the call in a serialized args structure. We'll send you the exact snippet but you should enable both for production-like behavior
02:05 Priya: ok, please send the snippet. On the latency spikes: when streaming is enabled we see median latency ~120ms per token but occasional jumps to 800-1200ms for some requests. If we disable streaming and use batch=8 we get more consistent 300-400ms but throughput drops
02:30 Diego: sounds like batching and the KV cache interactions; if your workload has many short prefixes streaming + small batch sizes can hit kernel warm-up and batching delays. Are you using prefix caching or the KV cache for repeated contexts?
02:45 Priya: we have a lightweight prefix cache in the app but not using Redwood KV cache explicitly yet. We didn't want to change too many variables during POC
02:58 Lin: another point: streaming relies on partial tokenization behavior and some runtime kernels can cause tail latency when context length crosses a compilation boundary. We can recommend a quantization/profile that reduces those spikes. We'll propose two profiles: low-latency (more memory, less quantization) and cost-optimized (more quant, larger batch tolerance)
03:20 Alison: from product side, our success criteria is: 95th percentile latency <500ms for interactive features and structured JSON success rate >99% over a representative prompt set
03:35 Maya: perfect, we'll aim for that. For the structured JSON success rate, Diego will run the schema-enforced snippet across your prompt set and send back pass/fail counts
03:48 Jared: quick note - logs attached to the shared drive (link dropped in chat) include two failing examples and the raw model output. The timestamps correspond to the test harness trace IDs
04:00 Diego: ok we'll take those and reproduce. Also, please include examples where streaming was on and off so we can compare traces
04:12 Priya: one small thing: in our Node SDK integration we saw the function-calling helper mutate the request headers and our auth layer started rejecting some calls intermittently. Might be unrelated, but worth flagging
04:25 Lin: hmm, that might be a wrapper ordering issue in middleware; can you share the exact SDK callstack? we can repro locally
04:36 Marco: we'll upload a minimal repro by Monday, should be straightforward
04:40 Diego: great. On the SDK snippet we recommend using the following flow: register function schema with the SDK API, call generateWithFunctions({functions, mode: 'strict', validateSchema: true, streaming: true}), and provide a onFunctionCall callback that returns a deterministic args object. That pattern reduces free-text emissions
05:05 Priya: if we use strict mode and auto-retry, do we risk hitting rate limits because of retries? we have a throughput target of 200 rps at peak during experiments
05:20 Maya: good question. Two mitigations: 1) increase client-side concurrency limits and implement exponential backoff for retries; 2) on Redwood side we can provision a dedicated test lane during the pilot to avoid tenant-level throttling. We'll propose a dedicated pool for your pilot window (subject to capacity)
05:40 Jared: is dedicated capacity necessary? we want to understand tradeoffs — cost vs predictability
05:50 Diego: dedicated helps with tail latency and predictable throughput because you avoid noisy neighbors and kernel eviction. For POC we can do a small reserved pool for the benchmarking window and revert to shared for baseline tests
06:05 Priya: ok that seems fine. For the schema problems, we also noticed that sometimes the model includes extraneous text before the JSON payload when using streaming which our parser doesn't handle well
06:20 Lin: yes streaming partial tokens can include preface text. Two fixes: 1) use the SDK's structured output buffer that waits for a complete json block before callback, 2) add a tolerant pre-parser that strips non-json prefix. We'll send both code approaches
06:40 Alison: can you give rough ETA on the fixes and the benchmark session?
06:45 Maya: Diego will send SDK snippet and instrumented tests by 2025-03-07; Priya will run tests and upload logs by 2025-03-12; Diego and Lin will run a joint benchmark on 2025-03-13 and share a short report by 2025-03-14
07:05 Jared: also curious about observability — can we get per-request token-level latency and cost breakdowns for our pilot? that's key for internal TCO discussions
07:15 Diego: yes Redwood Console can provide per-route token cost and latency; we'll request extended retention for the pilot traces and add you as viewers to the project in the console. We'll include exportable CSVs for your finance team
07:28 Priya: one last technical ask — is there a recommended JSON schema pattern for arrays of heterogeneous items? our item types can be string or object and our current schema validation is failing on union types
07:45 Lin: I'd recommend explicit discriminator fields (type: 'string' or 'object') so you can validate deterministically. If you prefer union-style, we can include a custom validator in the SDK that attempts each shape sequentially and reports best match
08:05 Marco: repro for the Node header mutation will be uploaded. Also we'll include traces showing KV cache misses if we flip to the Redwood cache
08:18 Maya: awesome. anything else from the customer side?
08:22 Priya: nothing else, just looking forward to the snippet and the benchmark session
08:28 Alison: thanks, we'll review the pricing options and circle back to Maya on commitment levels
08:35 Maya: thanks everyone, recap: Diego to send instrumented SDK snippet with streaming and strict function-call example and structured output validator; Priya to run tests and upload logs; Maya to share pricing; benchmark session scheduled for 2025-03-13.

Close: 08:45 meeting ends

Notes about transcription quality: medium — a few names were mis-recognized and there's occasional dropped punctuation; overall content aligns with call notes.
